reports.title: AMERICAS GOLD AND SILVER CORPORATION Condensed Interim Consolidated Financial Statements For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 (In thousands of U.S. dollars, unless otherwise stated, unaudited)

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Americas’ consolidated production guidance for 2026 is a range between 3.2 million and 3.6 million ounces of silver at an AISC range of $30 to $35 per ounce sold. The Company expects to achieve the low end of existing full-year production guidance and the high end of AISC guidance range.

desk.headline: Revenue up 68% to $51.4m on record silver output; 2026 seen at low end of production and high end of cost range
results: Revenue rose 68% to $51.4m on record silver output of 800,458 oz and a realised silver price of $60.54/oz.
Cosalá in Mexico drove the gain: silver output up 28% at an AISC of $25.21/oz; Galena in Idaho produced less silver at a much higher $60.07/oz.
The net loss narrowed to $5.6m ($0.02 a share), held back by $5.4m of income tax; adjusted EBITDA was $9.3m.
Spending on mines of $96.0m in nine months cut cash to $63.3m; liquidity is about $113m including an undrawn $50m loan tranche.
The remaining gold and silver delivery obligations were settled in Q2, largely with new shares; the accounts still carry a going-concern caution.

guidance.summary: The 2026 target stays at 3.2–3.6m oz of silver at an AISC of $30–35/oz, but the company now expects the low end for output and the high end for costs. Year-to-date AISC of $39.16/oz is above that range.

watch: Whether Galena's output rises and its costs fall as hoist and development work finishes.
Q4 silver output against the 3.2m oz low end of guidance.
Cash levels while capital spending stays heavy.
